adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() unconditionally even though getCredential may return Optional.empty(), causing NoSuchElementException and a 500 error page for users without a credential

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the code now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and then immediately calls `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(credentialModelOpt.get());` with no presence check. Since `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` returns `Optional<CredentialModel>` that can be empty (no federated or stored recovery-codes credential found), this can throw `NoSuchElementException` at runtime, resulting in a 500 error if the bean is instantiated for a user without the credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getCredential() prefers federated credentials and feeds the CredentialModel into RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(), which will hit a JSON parse exception if the storage returns a dummy model without full credentialData

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now checks `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` first and callers pass the resulting `CredentialModel` into `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(...)`. However, the claim that a federated credential will be a “dummy model without full credentialData” and that `createFromCredentialModel()` will therefore throw a JSON parse exception is not verifiable from this diff: `createFromCredentialModel()` is not shown, and the updated test user-storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage#getCredentials`) actually returns a fully populated recovery-codes credential model with JSON-backed data. So the asserted failure mode depends on external behavior not evidenced in the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes are never invalidated/consumed after successful validation for federated user-storage users (no updateCredential call post-validation), making them infinitely reusable and defeating one-time use

adjudication.rationale: In the added federated user-storage implementation (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage), recovery codes validation is implemented as a pure membership check and never consumes/removes the used code. Specifically, the new `isValid(..., input)` branch for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without updating `myUser.recoveryCodes` or calling any `updateCredential`/write-back to remove the matched code. This makes the same recovery code reusable indefinitely for federated users in this implementation, defeating one-time use semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes unhashed recovery codes into UserCredentialModel.challengeResponse sent to user storage, causing plaintext storage in contrast to the local hashed path

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the user-storage path builds a `UserCredentialModel` whose value/challengeResponse is `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` (the raw generated recovery codes) and calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. The included `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential` persists `input.getChallengeResponse()` directly into `CredentialModel.credentialData`, and `isValid` later deserializes that list and compares it directly to the provided code, confirming plaintext storage/validation for the federated/user-storage path. Meanwhile the local-storage path uses `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(..., credentialModel)` instead of the raw JSON, so the two paths store different representations and the federated path clearly stores unhashed codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials silently omits the credential on IOException, leaving inconsistent state where isConfiguredFor returns true but getCredentials returns nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials`, when `myUser.recoveryCodes != null` it attempts to deserialize `myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData()` via `JsonSerialization.readValue(...)`. On `IOException` it only logs `log.error(...)` and does not add any recovery-codes credential to `credentialModels`, returning a stream without that credential. However, `isConfiguredFor(...)` returns `true` whenever `myUser.recoveryCodes != null` (regardless of whether the data can be deserialized). This creates the inconsistent state described: configured=true but `getCredentials()` can omit the credential on deserialization failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials throws NPE for unknown users because getMyUser returns null and myUser.recoveryCodes is dereferenced

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage#getCredentials`, the diff adds `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` and then immediately dereferences `myUser` via `if (myUser.recoveryCodes != null) { ... }` and `if (myUser.otp != null) { ... }`. `getMyUser` returns `users.get(translateUserName(user.getUsername()))`, which can be `null` for unknown/unmapped users, leading to an NPE when `getCredentials` is called for such a user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes looks up by raw username while updateCredential stores under translateUserName(user.getUsername()), so the assertion can pass vacuously on key mismatch

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential(...)` stores recovery codes under `users.get(translateUserName(user.getUsername()))...`, while `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes(String username)` checks `userPasswords.get(username)` and returns `false` if missing. Even if there were a key mismatch, the new test calls `assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage(true)`, so a mismatch would cause the assertion to fail (not “pass vacuously”). Also, the diff does not show what `translateUserName(...)` does or how `userPasswords` relates to `users`, so the claimed mismatch is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential re-throws IOException without context (raw RuntimeException) losing user/realm/operation information for diagnosis

Recovery codes stored in plaintext in federated user storage via CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java ~192-196), while the local-storage path stores SHA-256 hashed codes

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, which serializes `generatedCodes` (a `List<String>` of recovery codes) into JSON and passes it as the `challengeResponse` in a `UserCredentialModel` to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential, the recovery-codes branch persists this value directly via `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`, and validation later deserializes and compares codes by equality, confirming the codes are stored and used in plaintext in federated storage. The claim that the local-storage path uses SHA-256 hashes is not directly verifiable from this diff, but plaintext storage in the federated path is clearly shown and is a security defect/regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes are never consumed/invalidated in user storage isValid (~323-341), allowing indefinite reuse of a single leaked code

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` the newly added Recovery Codes validation (`else if (input.getType().equals(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE))`) only deserializes the stored list and checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)` against the provided code. It never removes/updates the stored credential data on success, so the same recovery code can be reused indefinitely within this user storage implementation. This behavior is directly shown in the diff and matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Optional.get() called without presence check in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean constructor (~17-18) after refactor to RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user), risking NoSuchElementException

adjudication.rationale: In RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean, the refactor introduces `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without any presence check. If the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage, this will throw `NoSuchElementException` at runtime. The risk is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw-type deserialization of credential JSON with JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class), causing silent validation failure if element types aren't String

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds raw-type JSON deserialization with `JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class)` in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials()` and `isValid()` (and then compares elements via `key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())`). This is type-unsafe and would indeed lead to a quiet mismatch/failed validation if the stored JSON array contains non-String elements. However, the new write path in this diff serializes `List<String>` (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`), so with correct data it won’t fail; it’s primarily a robustness/type-safety issue rather than a clearly triggered defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Code-number mismatch: login bean presents a specific code position but isValid accepts any of the generated codes, leaving single-use semantics unenforced

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the UI/model selecting a specific recovery code slot via `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` (`getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get().getNumber()`), while the newly added federated user-storage validator in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` simply deserializes the stored JSON list and accepts *any* matching code (`generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`) without checking the requested code number or consuming/removing a used code. With `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` now preferring federated credentials, this mismatch is exercised for user-storage-backed users and undermines the intended per-code semantics (including single-use enforcement) for that storage implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential performs double credential-stream fetch on every lookup: getFederatedCredentialsStream is fully traversed and getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream is executed unconditionally on Optional.empty, doubling remote-storage round trips on a hot auth path

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` does `getFederatedCredentialsStream().filter(...).findFirst().or(() -> user.credentialManager().getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst())`. The second stream (`getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream`) is supplied via `Optional.or(Supplier)` and is only executed if the federated lookup returns empty, not “on every lookup” or “unconditionally”. While it can result in two lookups when the federated credential is absent, the finding’s claim of unconditional doubling/always-two round trips is not supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials allocates a new list and re-deserializes JSON on every call even though the backing MyUser is an in-memory singleton map, causing repeated deserialization within a single request

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(), the method builds a new ArrayList on each invocation and, when myUser.recoveryCodes != null, deserializes JSON every time via JsonSerialization.readValue(myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData(), List.class) before returning credentialModels.stream(). This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/efficiency concern (especially if getCredentials() is called multiple times during a request), but it does not demonstrate incorrect behavior or a functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential and BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid never consume/invalidate a used recovery code, allowing repeated reuse of the same recovery code to keep succeeding

adjudication.rationale: In the new user-storage support for recovery codes, BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() simply deserializes the stored List from credentialData and returns true if any element equals the provided code (`generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)`), but it never removes/updates the stored list to consume the used code. Separately, CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential() stores the full `generatedCodes` list JSON into a UserCredentialModel and, if `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` succeeds (user storage path), it does not invoke the dedicated recovery-code provider (which might otherwise handle one-time semantics). From the diff alone, recovery codes stored/validated via this user-storage path are reusable indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes for user-storage credentials are never invalidated/consumed — the federated login flow never burns a used code, so recovery codes can be reused indefinitely (single-use guarantee broken)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds support for storing recovery codes in user storage/federated credentials (e.g., `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` writes `generatedCodes` JSON into a `UserCredentialModel` and calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`). But for user-storage credentials, consumption/invalidation is not implemented: `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` only deserializes the stored JSON list and checks `anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without removing the matched code or updating the stored credential. No other diff hunk shows burning/rotating the codes after successful use for federated credentials, so codes would remain reusable indefinitely in user storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Contradictory credential-data format contract: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential writes a plain JSON list of raw codes to user storage, but read paths (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel) expect the serialized RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel format (hashed codes, usedCodes), causing parse failures for third-party providers

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializing `generatedCodes` as a JSON list and passing it via `UserCredentialModel(..., recoveryCodesJson)` into `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. The only concrete read/parse logic added/changed in this diff (e.g., `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials` and `.isValid`) also treats the stored data as a JSON list (`JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class)`) and wraps it into a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` via `createFromValues(...)`. The claim that read paths expect a different serialized model format (hashed/usedCodes) and will therefore fail is not verifiable from the diff (the internals/contract of `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel` are not shown), and the included user-storage provider implementation is consistent with the JSON-list storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded provider ID string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" in public SPI helper CredentialHelper instead of using RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID; if the constant changes, it silently returns null leading to NullPointerException on createCredential

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which hardcodes the provider id string in `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")` and then unconditionally calls `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` if user storage update fails. This is diff-grounded and creates a maintainability/robustness issue vs using a shared `PROVIDER_ID` constant (previously referenced in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction`). It’s not a verifiable current defect from the diff alone because we can’t confirm the constant’s value has changed or that the provider lookup can return null in this PR, but the hardcoding does increase the risk of a future NPE if the id diverges.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw plaintext recovery codes are exposed to the storage provider via updateCredential input, forcing user-storage providers to persist plaintext codes unlike the local hashed path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which serializes the newly generated raw recovery codes (`generatedCodes`) to JSON and passes them as the `challengeResponse` in a `UserCredentialModel` into `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. This means a federated/user-storage provider implementing `updateCredential` will receive the raw codes (and the included test provider `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential` persists `input.getChallengeResponse()` directly). However, the diff does not prove the system *forces* plaintext persistence—providers could still hash/encrypt before storing and validate accordingly—so it's a real security/architecture concern grounded in the change, but not a strictly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Swallowed deserialization error in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials: on IOException it logs without username and returns an empty/partial stream, so a user's recovery codes silently vanish from the credential list

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`, the new recovery-codes branch catches `IOException` from `JsonSerialization.readValue(...)`, logs only `"Could not deserialize  credential of type: recovery-codes"` (no username/user id), and then continues building the credentials list (adds OTP if present) and returns `credentialModels.stream()`. This means a deserialization failure results in recovery codes being omitted from the returned credential stream (partial/empty results) with only a generic log message, reducing observability and potentially masking issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validated recovery codes from user storage are never consumed/marked used after successful authentication, allowing federated users to reuse the same recovery code indefinitely (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential)

adjudication.rationale: In the added federated user-storage implementation, recovery codes are only stored (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential sets `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`) and validated (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid deserializes the stored JSON list and returns true if any entry equals the provided code). There is no code path in this diff that removes the used code from the stored list or updates `myUser.recoveryCodes` after a successful validation, so the same recovery code would continue to validate indefinitely for federated users of this storage provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw (unhashed) recovery codes are persisted as plaintext credential data for user storage via CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, diverging from the local provider's salted SHA-512 hashed storage

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the user-storage path serializes `generatedCodes` to JSON and puts it directly into `UserCredentialModel` as the `challengeResponse` (`new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`), then calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)`. The diff also updates the test user storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`) to persist `input.getChallengeResponse()` into `CredentialModel.setCredentialData(...)` and validates by deserializing the stored JSON and doing a direct equality check against the submitted code, i.e., plaintext storage/verification. Meanwhile, the non-user-storage path calls `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)`, which uses the provided `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` rather than the raw codes list. This demonstrates a real security/correctness divergence introduced by the change: federated/user-storage can end up persisting raw recovery codes instead of a hashed representation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Optional.get() called without presence check on credential lookup in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean constructor, risking NoSuchElementException and a raw 500 if the recovery credential is missing

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the constructor now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. If no recovery-codes credential exists in federated or local storage, this will throw `NoSuchElementException` and can surface as a 500. This is directly visible in the diff and the new `getCredential` API returns an `Optional` specifically because absence is possible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UserCredentialModel created with empty/blank credential ID and undocumented convention of placing raw codes JSON in challengeResponse, making the external SPI contract unreliable for provider implementations
matched_golden_ids: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel/UserCredentialModel is created without setting the stored credential ID, leading to null/blank getId() and downstream removal-by-id failures. The candidate explicitly flags an empty/blank credential ID (same core problem), though it also adds an additional concern about challengeResponse usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Swallowed deserialization errors in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials silently omit corrupted credentials, making tests mask real corruption rather than fail

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(), recovery codes are deserialized inside a try/catch. On IOException it only logs `log.error("Could not deserialize credential of type: recovery-codes")` and then continues, returning a stream that simply omits the recovery-codes credential (while still returning OTP). This behavior can hide/soften credential-data corruption in this testsuite provider instead of failing fast, which could reduce test sensitivity. It’s not strictly a product bug (this is a testsuite/backwards-compat provider), but it is a concrete, diff-introduced test robustness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bare RuntimeException(e) wrapping in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential loses failure context with no message or realm/user context

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, JSON serialization failures are caught and rethrown as `new RuntimeException(e)` with no message/context (`realm`, `user`, or operation), which makes diagnosing failures harder. This is visible in the added method: `catch (IOException e) { throw new RuntimeException(e); }` and there’s no additional logging or message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for the local-storage fallback path of createRecoveryCodesCredential in CredentialHelper.java:112-126; only the user-storage branch is exercised, so a fallback bug such as a provider-id string typo would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial branching logic in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`: it first tries `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` and only if that returns `false` does it fall back to `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes").createCredential(...)`. The new test `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` is explicitly aimed at user storage and asserts the credential exists in the user-storage provider (`hasRecoveryCodes("otp1")`), and the provider implementation returns `true` for recovery codes in `updateCredential(...)`, so this test exercises only the `userStorageCreated == true` branch. There is no test in the diff that forces `updateCredential(...)` to return `false` (e.g., a storage provider not supporting recovery codes) to validate the local-storage fallback path or catch issues like an incorrect provider-id string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that a used recovery code cannot be reused; BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential stores input.getChallengeResponse() as credentialData and isValid matches any code in the list, so a consumed code may remain valid forever — a real security-behavior gap

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds recovery-code support to the BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage test provider and a new test that only covers setup + a single login (testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin), but it does not test one-time/consumption semantics. In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...) for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE, validation is `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` with no removal/update of the list, so if no other component updates the stored credential after a successful use (not shown in this diff), a used code could remain valid. The finding’s core point (missing test + potential behavior gap in this provider’s implementation) is grounded in the shown code, but whether it is a real security defect in overall Keycloak behavior cannot be proven from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative test that a wrong/invalid recovery code fails authentication; the failure branches of BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid (recovery branch, lines 323-343) are never exercised, so a regression making isValid always return true would pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds recovery-code support to the backwards-compatibility user storage, including a new validation branch in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` with multiple failure paths (missing stored credential, JSON deserialization failure, and non-matching code). The only new test added (`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`) exercises the happy path by logging in with a valid generated recovery code, but there is no test asserting that an invalid/wrong recovery code fails authentication. Therefore, a regression where the recovery-code `isValid` branch erroneously returns `true` for any input would not be caught by the added test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitivity of code comparison is untested: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:341 uses raw String.equals while real provider compares hashed codes with normalized input, so the test verifies mock behavior rather than real-world behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` (new RecoveryAuthnCodes branch) deserializes a `List` and checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, which is a case-sensitive raw `equals`. However, the finding’s core claim that the “real provider compares hashed codes with normalized input” is not evidenced anywhere in this PR diff, so we cannot verify that the test is asserting behavior that diverges from production logic based on the diff alone. The “case-sensitivity is untested” assertion is also not a specific defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unit test for RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential lookup ordering (federated first, then local); the Optional-empty case causes RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:21 to call .get() and throw NoSuchElementException, untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new lookup logic in `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` (federated-first, then local via `.or(...)`). The added tests exercise recovery codes in user storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`) but do not specifically verify the ordering or the local-storage fallback behavior. Also, `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` now calls `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` and still unconditionally dereferences via `credentialModelOpt.get()`; while this can throw if no credential exists, the same risk effectively existed before (previous code did `.findFirst().get()`), so it’s more of an untested edge-case than a newly introduced, verifiable defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getCredentials in test provider double-wraps created-date and ignores stored values, and no test asserts that admin REST / account REST surface the recovery-codes credential for a federated user, unlike the OTP credential assertions

adjudication.rationale: The claim about `getCredentials` “double-wrapping created-date and ignoring stored values” is not verifiable from the diff: `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)` reads `myUser.recoveryCodes.getCreatedDate()` and `getUserLabel()` and passes them into `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, which appears to use the stored values rather than ignore them. However, the second part is diff-grounded: the newly added `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` only asserts storage-level presence via `hasRecoveryCodes("otp1")` and successful login, but unlike the existing OTP tests it adds no assertion that Admin REST or Account REST credential endpoints surface the `recovery-codes` credential for a federated user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plaintext recovery codes sent to federated user storage while local storage path stores hashed codes — security regression and inconsistent validation contract in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (~lines 112–127)

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the federated/user-storage path builds a `UserCredentialModel` whose challengeResponse is `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` (i.e., raw recovery codes JSON) and then calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)`. Only if that returns false does it fall back to `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)`, which is the normal provider-based creation path that could apply its own encoding/hashing/format contract. This diff therefore introduces a clear path where plaintext recovery codes are persisted into federated storage, bypassing provider logic, which is a security issue and creates a contract inconsistency between federated vs local creation paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Split-brain API: createRecoveryCodesCredential takes both credentialModel and generatedCodes, requiring callers to keep two parallel representations of the same credential in sync

adjudication.rationale: The new helper API `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(..., RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel credentialModel, List<String> generatedCodes)` (added in `CredentialHelper.java`) requires the caller to pass both a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` and a separate `generatedCodes` list. The method then persists `generatedCodes` (serialized JSON) when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` succeeds (user storage path), but persists `credentialModel` when falling back to local storage via `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)`. This is two parallel representations of the same logical credential, and the API relies on the caller keeping them consistent; a mismatch would store different data depending on the branch. This is a design/maintainability concern visible in the diff, not a guaranteed defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded provider id magic string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" in CredentialHelper.java:113 instead of using RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID constant, risking silent NPE if the id changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a hardcoded provider id string in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. There is no null-check before `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`, so the code becomes more fragile if the provider id ever changes or is unavailable. However, from the diff alone we cannot verify that the string is currently incorrect or that `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` differs, so it’s not a verifiable defect today—more a maintainability/robustness issue created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() without presence check on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, causing NoSuchElementException and raw 500 on login page

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the diff changes credential lookup to `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` but then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking `isPresent()` (or using `orElseThrow` with a controlled error). If `getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()` (no recovery-codes credential in federated or local storage), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` and can surface as a 500 when rendering the login bean.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw List.class deserialization in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials and isValid without generic type — unchecked and lossy, teaching an unsafe pattern in reference example code

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce raw `List.class` JSON deserialization in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`: `JsonSerialization.readValue(myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData(), List.class)` in `getCredentials(...)` and again in `isValid(...)`. This loses generic type information (should be something like `List<String>` via a `TypeReference`) and encourages an unchecked/weakly-typed pattern in a reference/backwards-compat provider. However, given the expected payload is a JSON array of strings (recovery codes), this is not necessarily a concrete runtime defect in this diff—more a maintainability/type-safety concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Semantically overloaded field: challengeResponse reused to carry serialized credential JSON payload, a type-boundary leak across the user-storage SPI (CredentialHelper and BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `challengeResponse` being used as a carrier for a serialized JSON payload: `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializes `generatedCodes` to JSON and passes it as the value in `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`, which is then handed to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. In the test user-storage provider, `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential` persists recovery codes via `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`, i.e., it expects that JSON blob in `challengeResponse`. This is a real, diff-grounded cross-layer coupling/design smell (providers must implicitly know the JSON encoding and that it arrives via `challengeResponse`), but the diff also updates retrieval/validation in that provider (`getCredentials` deserializes and `isValid` checks against the list), so there’s no verifiable broken behavior shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading return value name userStorageCreated from CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential means "user storage handled it" not "created", confusing contract on new public SPI surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` where `boolean userStorageCreated = user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential);` is used to decide whether to fall back to local storage. While the variable name could be debated (it reflects whether the user storage handled the update), this is a naming/style concern only; the logic and contract are still clear from the code path (`if (userStorageCreated) ... else ...`). No verifiable defect or substantive review issue is shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrating a user to storage-backed recovery codes never invalidates their existing local DB recovery-codes credential, leaving two live credentials of the same type and allowing old revoked codes to remain valid indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` returns `true`, creates recovery codes in user storage but does not remove any pre-existing local (Keycloak DB) `recovery-codes` credential of the same type. This can leave duplicate credentials in different stores. However, the finding’s stronger claim that this “allows old revoked codes to remain valid indefinitely” is not directly verifiable from the diff, because the updated lookup (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`) prefers federated credentials first, so the local one may not be used in the shown login path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateCredential() returning true is trusted as persisted with zero verification; a storage returning true without persisting makes createRecoveryCodesCredential skip the local-storage fallback, showing the user codes that are permanently invalid with no error

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, which decides whether to fall back to local storage purely based on the boolean return of `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` (see new method in `CredentialHelper`). If a user-storage provider incorrectly returns `true` without actually persisting, the local-provider `createCredential(...)` is skipped, and the generated codes would not be usable. However, from the diff alone this is not a verifiable defect in Keycloak core logic because `updateCredential`’s contract is to return success; a provider violating that contract would be the bug. So this is a real, diff-grounded robustness/contract concern rather than a confirmed functional bug in the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and stored by federated storages (no hashing contract), unlike the local path which hashes, creating a security exposure if the federated storage is compromised

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a federated-storage path for recovery codes that stores the *raw generated codes* serialized as JSON. In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, it serializes `generatedCodes` via `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` and passes that as the `UserCredentialModel` value to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. The updated federated test storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`) persists this directly (`setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`), and validation (`isValid`) deserializes the stored JSON list and compares plaintext (`anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`). Meanwhile, the non-federated fallback uses `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` without using `generatedCodes`, implying a different (likely non-plaintext) representation. This creates an actual security exposure for federated storages: recovery codes are stored/validated as plaintext in the federated provider path, so compromise of that storage reveals usable codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated recovery codes are never consumed on use in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, dropping single-use semantics and allowing infinite replay

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid` the newly added recovery-codes branch deserializes the stored list and only checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, but it never removes/marks the matched code as used nor updates `myUser.recoveryCodes`/federated storage. For federated recovery codes validated via this provider, this drops single-use semantics and allows the same code to be replayed indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IOException in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials is swallowed, omitting the recovery credential and degrading into a silent no-credential state causing NoSuchElementException in the login bean

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(), an IOException during JsonSerialization.readValue(...) is caught and only logged, and the recovery credential is not added to the returned stream (credentialModels). This can result in RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returning Optional.empty() for a user that actually has recovery codes stored but cannot be deserialized. RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean then immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get() without an isPresent() check, which would throw NoSuchElementException when the credential is omitted due to that swallowed deserialization error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hard-coded provider id string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID, risking runtime NoSuchProviderException if the id changes

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the provider is looked up via a hard-coded string: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. The diff also removes the earlier use/import of `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction`. This is a concrete maintainability/robustness issue because the lookup now depends on the literal matching the provider id; however, from the diff alone we cannot verify the factory constant’s value or that it will change, so it’s not a demonstrable current runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls .get() on the Optional from getCredential, throwing NoSuchElementException with a 500 instead of a proper error when the credential is absent

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the constructor now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` to build `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` (no presence check). If the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage, this will throw `NoSuchElementException` and likely surface as a 500 instead of a handled error/redirect.
